$comment: PreToolUse on Edit|Write, not UserPromptSubmit. §10.4 said UserPromptSubmit, and that was written
before the mechanism existed: UserPromptSubmit receives the user's prompt, which does not name a
file, while the whole briefing is keyed BY file path. PreToolUse is the only event that carries one.
REWRITTEN 2026-07-26 after discovering the hook had never worked. It passed "${TOOL_INPUT_FILE_PATH}",
which Claude Code does not substitute — it expanded to an empty string, the CLI printed its usage
line, and `|| true` swallowed the exit code. The payload arrives as JSON on STDIN. And a PreToolUse
hook's plain stdout is DISCARDED: the model reads permissionDecisionReason and nothing else, so even
a correct path would have produced silence. Both halves were wrong, so the briefing — founding
design §5's 'gold' — reached zero sessions from the day it shipped.
No `|| true` any more. hookCli.ts exits 0 on every failure by design, so a wrapper that hides
non-zero exits would only hide a crash — which is exactly how the original defect survived.
